title: Building Bédjondo’s heritage together
lede: ADEB LONODJI is the association of Bédjondo, in southern Chad, and of its diaspora: it works for all the town’s inhabitants and safeguards Bedjond heritage. This English section presents the association, the town and our advocacy; the full site is in French.

Who we are

The association of Bédjondo and its diaspora

ADEB LONODJI — Association for the Development and Mutual Aid of Bédjondo — is the organisation that promotes the values, heritage and history of the Bedjond people, whose home is Bédjondo, capital of the Mandoul Occidental department in the Mandoul province of southern Chad. The Bedjond are part of the wider Sara group. The association’s development work serves all the inhabitants of Bédjondo, whatever their origin. Founded through discussions that began in 1986 and officially recognised in 1995, the association held its first forum in Bédjondo in 2000, then a second in Bébopen in 2003, before being relaunched in 2026 with four pillars, twenty-one themes, two cross-cutting units and a public advocacy programme.

Read more about the association →

What we do

Four pillars

I — Memory, Culture & Heritage

Memory and heritage, living culture, research and knowledge: documenting oral tradition, the Bedjond language, the Kul iron currency, and building a Bedjond and Sara library.

II — Human Development & Livelihoods

Agriculture, livestock and food security; entrepreneurship and inclusive finance; environment and climate; water, sanitation and hygiene; energy, roads and urban planning; education, youth and training; women’s empowerment; health and nutrition; social protection and children; emergencies and risks.

III — Governance, Peace & Advocacy

Governance and advocacy, peace and cohesion, the network of experts and the diaspora, justice and human rights.

IV — Digital & Innovation

Connectivity and digital services, artificial intelligence and data, digital skills and entrepreneurship.

Advocacy

A town of probably over 15,000 people without a town’s infrastructure

Bédjondo grew from 4,344 inhabitants (1993 census) to 11,086 (2009) and very probably exceeds 15,000 today. It has a mayor and a council, but no reliable electricity, a water network that serves a single village and often stops for lack of fuel, no broadband, no proper streets or drains, unmaintained tracks to its cantons, a health centre without a laboratory and overcrowded schools. We have published eight advocacy briefs, each with a sourced diagnosis, specific requests to named recipients, and our own commitments. Each dispatch and each reply is dated on the impact dashboard.

Our eight briefs →

Vision 2030

The ODEB LONODJI project

On 28 September 2026, forty years after the first discussions of 1986, the association launched the ODEB LONODJI initiative: a project to give the Bedjond country a permanent organisation for research, documentation, territorial development, innovation, heritage and diaspora mobilisation by 2030. Six missions, six programmes, a roadmap and a white paper (working draft, in French). Read the summary in English →

How to help

Join, share your skills, spread the word

Members of the diaspora and friends of Bédjondo can join the association, coordinate one of the themes still open (see the list on the themes page), lead one of the pillars still without a Pillar Lead (programme-manager level; posts created on 28 September 2026, see the themes page), contribute to the first concrete projects (a community digital space powered by satellite and solar energy; solar lighting for the market), offer professional skills — planners, engineers, doctors, teachers, IT specialists — or simply relay our advocacy. The association does not collect dues or donations for now: it will do so only once its authorisation is confirmed and an account is open in its name, so please send no money to anyone on its behalf. Write to us and we will get back to you.
